mainTopic: Cancelling forbidden items in mixtures: תרומה leaven, fish ציר, and the flavor of the גיד הנשה
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a debate between אביי and רב דימי about a משנה in ערלה: how much plain dough is needed to cancel out תרומה leaven that fell into it. רב דימי reads the רישא as one hundred and one and the סיפא as one hundred. אביי then asks why strong leaven is not cancelled in one hundred and one. רב דימי is silent, and אביי suggests that שאור is different because its leavening power is so strong. רב דימי supports this with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching that not all measures are equal: fish ציר needs close to two hundred. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה lets ציר be cancelled at all because it is only 'sweat'. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of גיד הנשה. רב הונא explains how its flavor is measured, and the גמרא notes a תנא who holds that sinews give no flavor. Stories about רבי חנינא and רבי אמי follow, and the הלכה is set that sinews give no flavor. The amud ends with a new challenge: why isn't a cooked גיד הנשה cancelled by the majority?

steps.title: רב דימי: the clause means one hundred
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers אביי's earlier question. The clause of the משנה refers to a mixture of one hundred times the volume, not sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means with one hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי is answering a question אביי asked just before this. He says the משנה's clause is talking about one hundred times the volume.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says there is 'not enough to cancel out in one hundred and one.' אביי had asked whether that means as little as sixty. רב דימי says no: it means exactly one hundred, just one short of the needed amount.

keyTerms.meaning: With one hundred, meaning one hundred times the volume of the forbidden item

phrases.english: No, with one hundred.
phrases.notes: He is answering אביי's question from just before: the clause means one hundred times the amount, not sixty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question, which comes before this part of the text.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ratio the משנה's clause about 'not enough to cancel out in one hundred and one' refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to a mixture of one hundred times the volume.

steps.title: אביי objects: the first clause is already one hundred
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that since the רישא already deals with one hundred, the סיפא must be dealing with a different number, sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the first clause is talking about one hundred, the last clause must be talking about sixty!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב דימי's answer. He claims the רישא already covers the case of one hundred, so the סיפא should be about sixty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the two clauses of a משנה should not be saying the same thing about the same number. If the רישא already means one hundred, then the סיפא, which uses the same wording, must mean something less, sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
With sixty, meaning sixty times the volume

phrases.english: But since the first clause is with one hundred,
the last clause must be with sixty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that the clause means one hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא already uses this wording for one hundred, so reading the סיפא as one hundred too makes both clauses talk about the same number.

steps.title: אביי quotes the same-kind case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the רישא about wheat leaven of תרומה in wheat dough. It forbids the dough if the leaven makes it rise, or if the required nullifying amount is missing. He compares this stricter same-kind case with the earlier beans-and-lentils case.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the first clause teaches: How is it stricter when one type mixes with its own type? Wheat leaven of תרומה fell into plain wheat dough, and there is enough to make it rise. Whether or not there is enough plain dough to cancel it out in one hundred and one, the dough is forbidden. If there is not enough to cancel it out in one hundred and one, whether or not there is enough to make it rise, the dough is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes the same-kind case of the משנה as evidence for his objection. Both conditions here concern wheat leaven in wheat dough. The different-kind סיפא is the beans-and-lentils case quoted earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted רישא has two independent grounds for forbidding the dough: the leaven can make it rise, or the nullifying amount is missing. אביי compares this same-kind case with the different-kind beans-and-lentils case. If the same nullifying measure applied to both, what would make the first case stricter? He therefore argues that the latter case uses sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: One type mixed with the same type, like wheat with wheat
Sourdough leaven used to make dough rise
Enough to make the dough rise
To cancel out a forbidden item in a larger mixture

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate tests here: whether the leaven makes the dough rise, and whether there is enough plain dough to cancel it out. Failing either test makes the dough forbidden. Don't mix the two up.

phrases.english: As the first clause teaches:
To be strict with a type and its own type, how so?

phrases.aramaic: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁל חִטִּין שֶׁנָּפַל לְעִיסַּת חִטִּין,
phrases.english: Wheat leaven that fell into wheat dough,
phrases.notes: The leaven is תרומה and the dough is plain חולין.

phrases.english: and there is enough in it to make the dough rise,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: whether there is enough to cancel it out in one hundred and one,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: or there is not enough to cancel it out in one hundred and one, it is forbidden.
If there is not enough to cancel it out in one hundred and one,
whether there is enough to make it rise,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: or there is not enough to make it rise, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the text that backs up אביי's objection in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the רישא already deals with one hundred.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the משנה in ערלה (2:6) about wheat leaven of תרומה in wheat dough.

steps.title: Can both clauses mean one hundred?
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his objection: would both the רישא and the סיפא really be talking about one hundred?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are both the first clause and the last clause talking about one hundred?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sums up his challenge as a pointed question. It makes no sense for both clauses to mean the same one hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real request for information. It is a challenge: if both clauses use the same wording for the same number, the משנה would be saying one thing twice. רב דימי now has to explain how the two clauses differ.

phrases.english: Are both the first clause and the last clause with one hundred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the quote in step 3 and sharpens the objection from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's reading that the סיפא means one hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both clauses would then have the same number, which a משנה would not say twice.

steps.title: רב דימי: the first clause is 101, the last is 100
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the two clauses are about different numbers: the רישא is about one hundred and one, and the סיפא is about one hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the first clause is with one hundred and one, and the last clause is with one hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי defends his reading by giving each clause its own number. The רישא is about one hundred and one, and the סיפא is about one hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the רישא was about one hundred, which forced the סיפא down to sixty. רב דימי moves the רישא up to one hundred and one instead. Now the clauses no longer overlap, and the סיפא can still mean one hundred, just as he said in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי holds his ground: the סיפא means one hundred, not sixty. He avoids the overlap אביי pointed out by reading the רישא as one hundred and one.

phrases.english: No, the first clause is with one hundred and one,
and the last clause is with one hundred.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each clause a different number so they no longer overlap.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the רישא meant one hundred, so the סיפא would have to mean sixty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא means one hundred and one and the סיפא means one hundred, so רב דימי's reading of the סיפא stands.

steps.title: Why isn't strong leaven cancelled in one hundred and one?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if the mixture is one hundred and one, the תרומה should be cancelled. Why would leavening power make it forbidden? רב דימי has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is enough leaven in it to make the dough rise, why is it not cancelled in one hundred and one? He was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises a new problem with רב דימי's reading. The case is one where the שאור of תרומה is strong enough to make the dough rise, and he asks why one hundred and one would not cancel it. רב דימי cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that תרומה is cancelled in one hundred and one. רב דימי read the רישא as a mixture of one hundred and one, and in that reading the leaven still forbids the dough if it is strong enough to make it rise. אביי asks why leavening power should beat the normal cancelling ratio.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent; he had no answer

phrases.english: And when there is enough in it to cause leavening
in one hundred and one,
why is it not nullified?
He was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְחַמֵּץ בִּמְאָה וְחַד, אַמַּאי לָא בְּטִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב דימי's answer from step 5 that the רישא deals with one hundred and one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's reading that the רישא is about one hundred and one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה is normally cancelled in one hundred and one, so leavening power should not keep the mixture forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe leaven is different because it is so strong
steps.stepSummary: אביי himself suggests an answer: שאור may be different because its leavening power is very strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps leaven is different, because its leavening is strong.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב דימי is silent, אביי offers a possible answer to his own question: שאור is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that strong leaven can still affect a very large amount of dough. So the normal ratio of one hundred and one may not be enough to cancel it when it actually makes the dough rise.

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps
leaven is different,
because its leavening is potent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 after רב דימי's silence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the substance: leaven is an exception to the normal ratio
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every forbidden item should be cancelled in one hundred and one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strong leaven can still have an effect beyond one hundred and one, so it is not cancelled.

steps.title: Not all measures are equal: brine needs close to two hundred
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says אביי reminded him of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching that not all measures are the same, since fish ציר needs close to two hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You reminded me of something that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Not all the measures are equal, for brine has a measure close to two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי accepts אביי's idea and supports it with a teaching that some forbidden things need much more than the usual ratio to be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fish ציר needs close to two hundred, then one hundred and one is clearly not a fixed rule for everything. This supports the idea that strong שאור also follows its own measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Brine (the liquid that comes out of salted fish)

phrases.english: He said to him: You reminded me of a matter
that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
Not all the measures are equal,
for brine, its measure is close to two hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְכַּרְתַּן מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.raayaObject: That some forbidden things are not cancelled at the usual ratio
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement about ציר

steps.title: The source: the משנה about non-kosher fish brine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that is the source for brine: רבי יהודה says a רביעית of non-kosher fish brine forbids two סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The brine of a non-kosher fish is forbidden. רבי יהודה says: a רביעית in two סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the 'close to two hundred' figure comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סאה is 24 לוג, so two סאה are 48 לוג, which is 192 רביעיות. רבי יהודה's ratio of one רביעית in two סאה is therefore close to two hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: Two סאה, a large volume (48 לוג)

phrases.english: As we learned: A non-kosher fish, its brine is forbidden;
Rabbi Yehuda says: a quarter-log in two se'a.
phrases.notes: Two סאה equal 192 quarter-logs. That is the 'close to two hundred.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the משנה behind רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That brine needs close to two hundred to be cancelled
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי יהודה's view on non-kosher fish brine

steps.title: But רבי יהודה holds that a mixture of the same kind is never cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can let brine be cancelled at all, since he holds that מין במינו is not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי יהודה say: a type mixed with its own type is not cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the brine source: by רבי יהודה's own rule, the brine should never be cancelled at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds elsewhere that something mixed with the same kind of food is never cancelled. Non-kosher fish brine mixed with kosher fish brine looks like the same kind, so how can he give any ratio at all?

keyTerms.meaning: Something mixed with the same kind of food
But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabbi Yehuda say:
a type with its own type is not nullified?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מִין בְּמִינוֹ לֹא בָּטֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that brine is cancelled in two סאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה holds that מין במינו is never cancelled, so brine should not be cancelled at any ratio.

steps.title: Brine is only sweat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that brine is different because it is only 'sweat' of the fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Brine is different, because it is merely sweat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: brine does not count as the fish itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since brine is only liquid that sweats out of the fish, it does not have the full status of the fish. So רבי יהודה's rule that מין במינו is never cancelled does not apply to it.

phrases.english: Brine is different,
because it is merely sweat.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the substance: brine lacks the full status of the fish
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Brine counts as the fish, so מין במינו should never be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: Brine is only sweat, so it can be cancelled at a large ratio.
steps.whatToRemember: The cancelling ratio is not always one hundred and one. Strong שאור and fish ציר each follow their own measure.

steps.title: How the flavor of the sinew is measured
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה's words 'how do we measure' and רב הונא explains: like meat cooked with turnip heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we measure? רב הונא said: Like meat with turnip heads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה of גיד הנשה, which asks how we check whether the sinew gives flavor to the thigh. רב הונא explains the measuring method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sinew's flavor cannot be tasted directly, since the sinew and the thigh are both meat. So we picture it as meat cooked with turnip heads: if that much meat would flavor the turnips, the thigh is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The forbidden sciatic nerve (the topic of the משנה)

phrases.english: How do we measure?
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה about the גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Like meat with turnip heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of ratios and returns to the words of the משנה about גיד הנשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We measure the sinew's flavor as if it were meat cooked with turnip heads.

steps.title: Our משנה disagrees with the view that sinews give no flavor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה does not follow רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who says sinews give no flavor at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: Sinews do not give flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another תנא disagrees with our משנה's whole idea of measuring the sinew's flavor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה assumes the גיד can give flavor, which is why it must be measured. רבי ישמעאל holds that sinews give no flavor at all, so by his view there would be nothing to measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving flavor to the food around it
A sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
Sinews do not impart flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the measuring method of step 12 by noting a תנא who rejects the idea of the sinew's flavor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה holds that sinews give flavor, which goes against רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that measuring the גיד's flavor depends on the view that sinews give flavor at all. The view that they do not is a real disagreement.

steps.title: A man asks רבי חנינא and is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A man asks רבי חנינא a question and is told his food is permitted. רבי יהודה בר זבינא, sitting at the gate, asks him what the answer was.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came to רבי חנינא with a question. רבי יהודה בר זבינא was sitting at the gate. When the man came out, רבי יהודה בר זבינא asked him what רבי חנינא had said. The man answered: he permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a real ruling. This first part sets up the story: the man is told his food is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In context the question is about meat cooked with its sinew still inside. רבי חנינא permitted it, which fits the view that sinews give no flavor. The story continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: before him (coming to a sage with a question)
at the gate / at the door

phrases.english: A certain man came before Rabbi Chanina,
phrases.notes: The story doesn't spell out the question, but from the topic it was about meat cooked with its sinew inside.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִינָא אַבָּבָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevina was sitting at the gate.
When the man came out, he said to him:
What did he tell you?
He said to him: He permitted it to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story connected to the view from step 13 that sinews give no flavor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא permitted the man's food.

steps.title: רבי חנינא firmly says sinews give no flavor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר זבינא sends the man back to ask again. רבי חנינא is annoyed and sends back the answer: sinews give no flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר זבינא told the man to go back and ask רבי חנינא again. רבי חנינא said: Who is bothering me? Go tell the one sitting at the gate: sinews do not give flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי חנינא clearly stating his reason: sinews give no flavor at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בר זבינא thought there might be a mistake, so he sent the man back. רבי חנינא's reply shows he permitted it on purpose, because he holds like רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. Since the sinew adds no taste, the meat around it stays permitted.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go back and bring it before him again.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה בר זבינא speaking. He suspects רבי חנינא may not have understood the question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: מַאן הַאי דְּקָא מְצַעַר לִי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: Who is this who is bothering me?

phrases.aramaic: זִיל אֵימָא לֵיהּ לְמַאן דְּיָתֵיב אַבָּבָא:
phrases.english: Go tell the one who is sitting at the gate:
Sinews do not give flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 14 and gives רבי חנינא's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sinews do not give flavor, so the meat cooked with them is permitted.

steps.title: רבי אמי sends questioners to a lenient sage
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי did not hold the lenient view himself, but he sent people to רבי יצחק בן חלוב, who permitted it in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came to רבי אמי with this question, he sent them to רבי יצחק בן חלוב. That sage ruled it permitted, in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי אמי himself did not agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about this question. רבי אמי passes the question to a sage who rules leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the lenient view had serious support, going back to רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי אמי did not hold this way himself, but he did not stop others from relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: he does not hold that way

phrases.english: When people came before Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁדַּר לְהוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן חֲלוּב,
phrases.english: he would send them before Rabbi Yitzchak ben Chalov,
who would rule that it is permitted
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
but he himself did not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story showing more support for the lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יצחק בן חלוב permitted it in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. רבי אמי himself did not agree.

steps.title: The final ruling: sinews give no flavor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is that sinews give no flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: sinews do not give flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on this topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though our משנה did not hold this way (step 13), the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, רבי חנינא, and רבי יהושע בן לוי. In practice, a sinew does not make the food cooked with it forbidden through its taste.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה is אין בגידין בנותן טעם: sinews give no flavor, even though our משנה assumed they do.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not make the גיד הנשה itself permitted to eat. It only means its taste does not forbid the other food cooked with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling: meat cooked with the גיד הנשה inside is permitted once the גיד is removed.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: sinews do not give flavor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute shown in steps 13 through 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that sinews give no flavor.

steps.title: Why isn't the cooked sinew cancelled by the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a גיד הנשה cooked with other sinews and asks why it is not simply cancelled by the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a גיד הנשה that was cooked. The גמרא asks: let it be cancelled by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and right away raises a challenge against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the גיד הנשה is cooked with other sinews and you can't tell which one it is, all of them are forbidden. The גמרא asks why. There is one forbidden sinew and many permitted ones, so the forbidden one should be cancelled by the majority (רוב).

keyTerms.meaning: the forbidden sinew of the thigh

phrases.english: A gid hanasheh that was cooked.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. It is about the גיד הנשה cooked together with other sinews, where you can't tell which one is forbidden.

phrases.english: Let it be cancelled by the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the flavor discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that all the sinews are forbidden when the גיד הנשה cannot be identified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One forbidden item mixed into a majority of permitted items is normally cancelled by רוב, so the other sinews should be permitted.
